title: Volcano and tsunami diagram sheet
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y9 lesson 23 (Volcano and tsunami diagram sheet (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 23: Tsunami! What is a volcano? Mount St Helens. To understand how tsunamis form and how volcanoes erupt, using real examples

picture.alt: Mount St Helens after the eruption
picture.draw: Draw and label: Volcano and tsunami diagram sheet

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Magma rose; the north side bulged outwards

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: A magnitude 5.1 earthquake shook the volcano

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: The bulge collapsed in a giant landslide

parts.label: Step 4
parts.text: Pressure released in a sideways blast and ash column

questions.q: What is the difference between magma and lava?
questions.a: Magma is underground; lava has reached the surface
questions.model: Molten rock underground is magma. When it comes out it is called lava. Same rock, different place.

questions.q: When did Mount St Helens erupt?
Which area was worst hit in 2004?
Draw a labelled composite volcano and a tsunami formation diagram; then write a case study paragraph on Mount St Helens.
questions.a: Accurate diagrams; paragraph with date, place, sequence and effects
questions.model: Teacher labels the magma chamber and vent first.

questions.q: Why did the 2004 tsunami kill so many people far from the earthquake?
questions.a: No warning system, crowded low coasts, waves crossed the ocean in hours

questions.q: How do warning systems reduce tsunami deaths today?
questions.a: Sea-floor sensors and buoys detect waves; alerts and evacuation routes

questions.q: Big question: how can an undersea quake destroy a distant coast?
questions.a: It lifts the sea bed, sending fast waves across the ocean that grow tall near shore
